summary: Geoff Childs is an anthropologist and Tibetologist. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, studying under Tsetan Chonjore. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at Australian National University and was Assistant Professor of Anthropology at Washington University in St. Louis.

Geoffrey Barstow is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche, earning degrees from Kathmandu University and the University of Virginia. He held posts at the University of Virginia and Oregon State University.

Geoffrey Goble is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Virginia and completed his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington. In 2019, he was Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Oklahoma.

Geoffrey Samuel is a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Cambridge under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, Peter J. Wilson, and Edmund Leach. His posts include professorships at the University of Newcastle, Lancaster University, and Cardiff University.

Georg Buddruss was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate under Paul Thieme at Goethe University Frankfurt and studied at the University of Tübingen. He was a professor at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1963–1995).

Georg Bühler was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen. He served as a professor in the Bombay Presidency and at Elphinstone College, and later held a chair at the University of Vienna from 1880.

Georg Christoph Lichtenberg was a philosopher and scholar who studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1763 to 1769. He subsequently held a post at the University of Göttingen from circa 1769 until 1799.

Georg Curtius was a linguist who studied under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, Christian Lassen, Franz Bopp, and August Wilhelm von Schlegel in Bonn and Berlin. He held professorships of classical philology at Charles University, Kiel University, and the University of Leipzig (1862–1885).

Georg Forster was an Indologist and scholar who attended Saint Peter's School. He held academic posts at Vilnius University from 1784 to 1787 and at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz from circa 1788 to 1793.

Georg Freytag was a linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He served as a sub-librarian at the University of Königsberg and as Professor of Oriental Languages at the University of Bonn from 1819 to 1861.

Georg Friedrich Grotefend was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was educated at the Lessing-Gymnasium from circa 1792 to 1795 and studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1795 to 1797.

Georg Huth was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig from circa 1885 to 1889 and later held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1891 to 1906.

Georg Kaibel was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. During his career, he held academic posts at the University of Rostock, the University of Breslau, the University of Greifswald, and the University of Göttingen.

Georg Ludolf Dissen was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1804 to 1807, and later held posts at the University of Marburg (circa 1812–1813) and the University of Göttingen (circa 1813–1837).

Georg Martin Dursch was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tübingen and under Antoine-Léonard Chézy at the University of Paris. In 1829, he became a professor at Johann-Vanotti-Gymnasium Ehingen.

Georg Morgenstierne was a linguist specializing in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Sten Konow, Heinrich Lüders, and Wilhelm Schulze, and held professorships at the University of Gothenburg (1930–1937) and the University of Oslo (1937–1962).
Georg Simmel was a philosopher. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1876 to 1881 and later held a post at the same institution from circa 1885 until 1914.

Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel was a philosopher who studied at the Tübinger Stift, the University of Tübingen, and the University of Jena under Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling. He held posts at the universities of Jena, Heidelberg, and Berlin.

Georg von Simson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Mainz and the University of Göttingen. He served as an editor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and was a professor at the University of Oslo (1977–2003).

Georg von der Gabelentz was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and linguistics. Educated at Jena, TU Dresden, and Leipzig, he served as professor of East Asian languages at the University of Leipzig (1878–1889) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1889).
